Rashi on Shabbat 113a:10:1.hebrew: לפי שאין ניטלין - אף בחול מפני כובדן, הלכך כל מלאכתן לכך:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:10:1.english: Because they are not carried - Even during the week, because of their weight; therefore, all their work is for that [purpose].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:1.hebrew: מקפלין את הכלים - בגדים, כשפושטן מקפלין, מפני שמתרככין מכיבוסם ומתקמטי' כשאינן מקופלים:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:1.english: One may fold the articles - [Meaning] garments; when one takes them off, one folds them, because they become softened from their laundering and become wrinkled when they are not folded.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:2.hebrew: אפי' ד' או ה' פעמים - כדי לחזור וללובשן בו ביום:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:2.english: Even four or five times - in order to put them on again on that same day.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:3.hebrew: מיוה"כ לשבת - כגון אם חל יוה"כ להיות בע"ש:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:3.english: From Yom Kippur for Shabbat - For example, if Yom Kippur falls on Shabbat eve [Friday].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:4.hebrew: קריבין ביוה"כ - שחל להיות במוצאי שבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:11:4.english: [They] are offered on Yom Kippur - when it falls on the conclusion of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:12:1.hebrew: בשני בני אדם - כשמקפלין אותן, מפשטין קמטיהן ונראין כמתקנין:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:12:1.english: With two people - When they fold them, they smooth out their creases and appear as if repairing [them].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:12:2.hebrew: ישנים - קיפולן מתקנן יותר מן החדשים, שהחדשים קשין מאליהן ואין ממהרין לקמוט:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:12:2.english: Old [garments] - Folding them improves them more than new ones, for new ones are stiff on their own and do not wrinkle quickly.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:12:4.hebrew: יש לו - אחרים להחליף היום, לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:12:4.english: [If] he has - other [garments] to change into today, [he may] not [fold them].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:13:1.hebrew: כלי לבן שלהן - רבותא נקט, וכל שכן צבועים:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:13:1.english: Their white garments - [It] stated a stronger case, and all the more so dyed [garments].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:13:2.hebrew: יש לו להחליף יחליף - מי שיש לו בגדים לבד מאותן שלבש בחול, יחליפם בשבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:13:2.english: [If] he has [garments] to change [into], he should change - One who has garments other than those that he wore on a weekday should change into them on Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:13:3.hebrew: ישלשל בבגדיו - כלפי מטה, שיראו ארוכים. והוא מדת עשירים היושבים בביתם ואינם צריכים לסלק בגדיהם מן הארץ בשביל מלאכה, וכבוד שבת הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:13:3.english: He should let his garments hang down - [That is,] downward, so that they appear long. And this is the manner of wealthy people who sit in their homes and do not need to lift their garments off the ground because of work, and it is [in] honor of Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:14:1.english: My honors - For they honor their owner.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:14:2.english: That your walking should not be, etc. - [The Gemara] explains them later on.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:14:3.hebrew: ממצוא חפצך - כי ההוא דאמרינן בעירובין (דף לח:), לא יטייל אדם לסוף שדהו בשבת לידע מה היא צריכה [אחר השבת]:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:14:3.english: From pursuing your affairs - Like that [statement] that we say in Eruvin (38b): A person may not walk to the end of his field on Shabbat in order to know what it needs [after Shabbat].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:14:4.english: Affairs of Heaven are permitted - For example, pledging charity and arranging [marriage] matches for children to be betrothed (below, Shabbat 150a).

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:1:1.hebrew: חדא מינייהו - אחד מן הראשים, [ולל"א] חד מיניהו מבטל ליה. כשיוציא הבהמה, לא יתיר אלא תחתון ויוציאנה בדוחק:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:1:1.english: One of them - One of the ends [of the rope]; [and according to another version,] one of them he voids [i.e., leaves permanently tied]: when he takes the animal out, he will untie only the lower one and take it out with difficulty.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:1:2.hebrew: מכלל דפליגי - בתמיה, ואמאי איפלגו? הא דמי להנך דלעיל:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:1:2.english: By inference, they disagree - [This is asked] in astonishment: why would they disagree? Behold, this is similar to those [cases] above.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:2:1.hebrew: קושרין דלי בפסקיא - ע"פ הבור, דפסקיא לא מבטל [ליה] התם:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:2:1.english: One may tie a bucket with a belt - Over the mouth of the cistern, for [one] does not leave a belt permanently there.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:2:2.hebrew: אבל לא בחבל - דמבטל ליה התם, והוי קשר של קיימא, שהרי קשור ותלוי שם תמיד:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:2:2.english: But not with a rope - Because he leaves it there [permanently], and it is a permanent knot, since it is tied and hanging there always.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:2:3.english: And Rabbi Yehuda permits [it] - [This is] explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:3:1.hebrew: בחבל דגרדי - פליגי, דצריך לה ולא מבטל לה:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:3:1.english: Regarding a weaver's rope - They disagree, for he needs it and does not leave it permanently.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:4:1.english: The rope of a bucket that was severed - in its middle.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:4:2.english: One may not tie [it] - For it is a permanent knot, [intended to last] forever.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:4:3.hebrew: כורך עליו - מחבר שני ראשי הפיסוק זה על זה, וכורך עליהם פונדא — אזור חלול — או פסיקיא — פיישול"א:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:4:3.english: One wraps around it - [He] joins the two ends of the severed [rope] one upon the other, and wraps around them a punda — a hollow belt — or a pesikya — [Old French:] faissole [a band or sash].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:4:4.hebrew: ובלבד שלא יענבנו - לחבל, דר"י סבר גזרינן עניבה אטו קשירה, ורבנן לא גזרו:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:4:4.english: As long as he does not tie it into a bow - [Referring] to the rope, for Rabbi Yehuda holds [that] we decree [a prohibition against] tying a bow on account of tying [a regular knot], whereas the Rabbis did not decree [this].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:6:1.hebrew: מיחלף - אינו ניכר בין זה לזה, ואי שרינן בדגרדי, אתי למישרי בדעלמא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:6:1.english: May be confused - One is not distinguishable from the other, and if we permit [it] with a weaver's [rope], one will come to permit [it] with an ordinary [rope].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:7:1.hebrew: וקושרו בפרה - ראשו אחד, והשני באבוס. ולא חיישינן שמא כשיתיר הפרה לא יתיר אלא הקשר שבראשה, ויבטל החבל באבוס שיהא מוכן לכך, או יתיר שבאבוס ויבטל אותו שבפרה, ונמצא האחד של קיימא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:7:1.english: And tie it to a cow - one end of it [to the cow] and the other to the trough. And we are not concerned lest when he unties the cow he will untie only the knot at its head and leave the rope [permanently] at the trough so that it will be ready for this [purpose], or [that] he will untie [the knot] at the trough and leave the one on the cow [permanently], and thus one [of the knots] will turn out to be permanent.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:1.hebrew: כלי קיואי - כלי אורגים, ואיידי דאיירי בחבל דגרדי נקט לה הכא:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:1.english: Weaver’s tools - Tools of weavers; and since [the Gemara] was discussing a weaver’s rope, it mentioned this here.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:2.hebrew: מותר לטלטלן - לשני הקנים לתשמיש אחר, ואשמעינן דאין גרדי מקפיד עליהם, ולא הוי מלאכתן לאיסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:2.english: May be moved - [Referring] to the two rods, for another use; and [this] teaches us that a weaver is not particular about them, and they are not [utensils whose] work is for a forbidden purpose.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:3.english: The upper and the lower beam - ensubles [Old French for the loom beams].

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:4.hebrew: מהו - מי אמרינן, איידי דיקירי לא חזו סתמייהו לתשמיש אחרינא, והוה ליה דבר שמלאכתו לאיסור:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:4.english: What [is the ruling] - Do we say [that] since they are heavy, they are ordinarily not fit for another use, and it is an object whose [primary] function is for a forbidden [activity]?

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:5.hebrew: ורפיא בידיה - רפויה היתה התשובה בפיו, אם לאסור אם להתיר:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:5.english: And it was weak in his hand - The answer was weak [i.e., uncertain] in his mouth, whether to forbid [or] whether to permit.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:6.hebrew: העמודים - טריור"ש בלע"ז, אותם המנוקבות שאורגין בהן הנשים:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:8:6.english: The posts - Triors in Old French, those perforated [posts] with which women weave.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:9:1.hebrew: דקא עביד גומא - כשחולצן מן הארץ, שהן תחובות בגומא, מזיז העפר ועביד גומא מקום העמוד:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:9:1.english: That he makes a hole - When he pulls them out of the ground, as they are inserted in a hole, he moves the earth and makes a hole [in] the place of the post.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:9:3.english: He need not be concerned - Because it has not taken root.

Rashi on Shabbat 113a:9:4.hebrew: ולא משום מעשר - להיות בטילה בנטיעה זו, וכשנוטלה יצטרך לחזור ולעשר:
Rashi on Shabbat 113a:9:4.english: Nor due to tithes - [For it] to become nullified by this planting, and when he takes it [out] he would need to tithe [it] again.

Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:12:1.hebrew: אבל יש לו להחליף לא - ולנו שיש לנו להחליף — אסור. ומסתפק ר"י אי קרי "יש לו להחליף" כשאין לו יפה כזה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:12:1.english: However, [if] he has [another garment] to change [into], no - And for us, who have [other garments] to change [into], [folding] is forbidden. And Ri is uncertain whether it is considered "he has [another garment] to change [into]" when he does not have one as nice as this:

Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:13:1.hebrew: מקפלים כלים כו' - מכאן למדנו דאסור לקפל טליתות של ב"ה, לפי שהם צורך מחר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:13:1.english: One folds garments, etc. - From here we learn that it is forbidden to fold tallitot of the synagogue, because they are needed for tomorrow.

Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:2:1.hebrew: כלל אמר ר"י - תימה: היכא קאי? אי אמילתיה קמייתא — התם מתיר לגמרי, והכא קתני "אין חייבין עליו", משמע הא איסורא איכא, כדדייק הש"ס לעיל. וי"ל דה"ק: כל קשר שאינו של קיימא — אין חייבין עליו, הא של קיימא — חייבין עליו, ואפי' עניבה; לאפוקי מדרבנן, דאמרו עניבה לאו היינו קשירה. א"נ, אמאי דקתני ברישא "אין חייבין עליהם" קאי רבי יהודה:
Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:2:1.english: "Rabbi Yehuda stated a principle" - This is astonishing: to what is [Rabbi Yehuda] referring? If [he is referring] to his first statement — there he permits [it] completely, whereas here [the Mishnah] teaches "one is not liable for it," which implies that there is a prohibition, as the Gemara infers above. And one can answer that this is what he is saying: Any knot that is not permanent, one is not liable for it; [implying that for] one that is permanent, one is liable for it, and even [for] a bow — to exclude [the opinion] of the Rabbis, who said that a bow is not [considered] tying. Alternatively, Rabbi Yehuda is referring to that which was taught in the earlier clause [of the Mishnah], "one is not liable for them."

Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:7:1.hebrew: התם חבל דעלמא הכא חבל דגרדי - וקמ"ל רב דלא גזרינן חבל דגרדי אטו חבל דעלמא, וכר' יהודה. א"נ, אפי' רבנן מודו דאפי' בחבל דעלמא לא שכיח שיהיה קשר של קיימא כשקושרו בפרה ובאבוס, ולהכי לא גזור בחבל דגרדי:
Tosafot on Shabbat 113a:7:1.english: There [it is] an ordinary rope; here [it is] a weaver's rope - And Rav teaches us that we do not decree [against] a weaver's rope on account of an ordinary rope, [in accordance] with Rabbi Yehudah. Alternatively, even the Rabbis agree that even with an ordinary rope, it is not common for it to be a permanent knot when one ties it to a cow and to a trough, and therefore they did not decree [against] a weaver's rope.
